born.why: The code prioritizes starvation avoidance, then uses a consensus of past experiences (global vs. specific poison rates) to make safer decisions than the original, reducing false positives on new fruits in dangerous environments while remaining aggressive when hungry and safe.

This code prioritizes survival by treating starvation as the primary threat, using past similar traits (smell/color/shape) to infer safety of unknown fruits, and switching to cautious exploration only when healthy.

It prioritizes immediate survival by eating when starving, avoids poisonous fruits by remembering past harms or shared traits, and efficiently carries known safe species while cautiously taste-testing unknowns only when hunger is low enough to afford the risk.

The code prioritizes survival by following instinct when starving, avoids poisonous fruits based on past negative experiences ('harmed'), and distinguishes between tasting new species for information and carrying known safe species to the pantry for efficiency.

The code prioritizes survival by learning from past bites (diary): if a fruit's traits (key, smell, color) match previous poisonous instances, it is avoided; if they match previous safe instances, it is eaten immediately. If no history exists or the fruit is ambiguous, she tastes it to gather data unless starvation is imminent (>80 hunger), in which case she eats to avoid dying of hunger, balancing risk against immediate need.

The code prioritizes carrying the target fruit, uses starvation thresholds to force eating/tasting when desperate, and leverages diary history to avoid poisonous species or traits while safely exploring unknown fruits via tasting when hunger allows.
